title: Minang Geopark Run 2026 Review: What the 2026 Race Was Like
seo_title: Minang Geopark Run 2026 Review: Bukittinggi Course, Cut-offs, Times
meta_description: Minang Geopark Run 2026 review: roads and trail sections from Jam Gadang, 19°C at the 6am start, a four-hour half-marathon cut-off and a slow field: median 3:05.
dek: What the 1 November 2026 race in Bukittinggi was like: the mixed road and trail course, the cool, wet air at 930 m, aid stations and cut-offs, and how the half-marathon and 10 km fields ran against them.
verdict: Enter if you want a scenic, hilly race in the West Sumatra highlands and are happy to run slowly. The 2026 race started beside Jam Gadang in Bukittinggi, at about 930 m, with several trail sections on the half marathon. It was 19°C with 98% humidity at the 6am start, and a little rain fell in the second hour. The field of 723 half-marathon and 916 10 km finishers was slow: the median half marathoner took 3:05, and one in eight finished in the last quarter of an hour before the four-hour cut-off. Only 4% of half marathoners broke two hours.

sections.heading: The Course: Highland Roads With Trail Sections
paragraphs: The race starts and finishes on Jalan Perintis Kemerdekaan in Bukittinggi, beside the race village at Jam Gadang, the city's clock tower [1]. The race is part of the Geopark Run Series and is set in the Sianok–Maninjau geopark of the West Sumatra highlands; 2026 was its eighth year and the second race of the 2026–2027 series, after Ijen [2].

The half marathon and 10 km are mostly on paved roads but include trail sections where the surface changes; the 5 km stays on roads [1]. Running clubs quoted by the organiser call the course challenging but beautiful, with geopark scenery along the way [3]. Train on hills and on uneven ground, and use shoes you trust off the tarmac.

sections.heading: The Weather: Cool, Saturated and Showery
paragraphs: Open-Meteo's historical model for central Bukittinggi, at 935 m, gives 19°C at 6am on race morning, with a dew point of 19°C, 98% humidity and almost no wind [4]. It warmed slowly, to 21°C at 7am, 22°C at 9am and 24°C with 85% humidity at 10am, when the half marathon closed. The model has light rain between about 7am and 10am, under a millimetre an hour [4].

These are modelled figures, used because the nearest airport, Padang, is at sea level and much hotter. The air is cooler than on the coast but almost fully saturated, so sweat barely evaporates. Expect wet surfaces on the trail sections if the showers come again.

sections.heading: Aid Stations and Cut-offs
paragraphs: The organiser promised water about every 2.5 km, and the race centre opened at 5.30am, with a bag drop for runners wearing a bib [5]. The official results show the half marathon starting at 6am, the 10 km at 6.30am and the 5 km at 6.45am [6].

The cut-offs were four hours for the half marathon, two and a half hours for the 10 km and an hour and a half for the 5 km [7]. For this field they bite. In the half marathon, 92 of the 723 finishers, or 13%, came in during the last 15 minutes before the four-hour limit, and three were outside it. In the 10 km, 68 finished in the last 15 minutes and 14 (1.5%) after the limit [6].
Finishers received a medal, an e-certificate and refreshments; half marathoners also got a finisher jersey [5].

sections.heading: How Fast the Field Is
paragraphs: The official results list 723 half-marathon and 916 10 km finishers; the 5 km is not included [6].

The half marathon was won in 1:24:12, and the top ten finished between 1:24 and 1:49. The median finisher took 3:05:12; only 4% broke two hours, 19% broke two and a half, and 90% were done by 3:47:54. Women were 15% of finishers, and the fastest woman ran 1:41:48 [6].
In the 10 km the top ten ran 38:37 to 51:31, the median was 1:39:41, only 2% broke an hour and 90% were done by 2:13:12. Women were 31% of 10 km finishers [6].

Those are slow times, which reflects the hills, the trail sections and a field of mostly recreational runners. Prize money goes to the top three men and women in each distance, from Rp13 million for the half-marathon winner down to Rp2 million for third in the 5 km [8]; the top ten in the half marathon all ran under 1:49.

sections.heading: Race Weekend Logistics
paragraphs: Race packs were collected on Friday 30 October, 2pm to 7pm, and Saturday 31 October, 9am to 7pm. There was no collection on race day and no posting of packs; a friend could collect with a signed authorisation and a copy of your ID [5]. Parking near the start was limited [5].

For runners flying in, the organiser arranged a DAMRI bus from Minangkabau International Airport and from the Masjid Raya Sumatera Barat in Padang to Pasa Ateh in Bukittinggi, at 11am and 4pm on the Friday and Saturday, for Rp45,000 a person [9].
Entry fees cannot be refunded, and categories and jersey sizes cannot be changed after payment [5].

sections.heading: Should You Enter the Next Minang Geopark Run?
paragraphs: Yes, if you want a highland race with scenery, cooler air than the coast and a big turnout of running clubs. A runner who can go under two hours for a road half marathon is near the front here.

Think twice if you are not used to hills or trail surfaces and expect to be close to three and a half hours: one in eight half-marathon finishers in 2026 was racing the four-hour clock at the end. Check the next date with the organiser before booking travel.
This review draws on the organiser's race information, modelled weather data and the official results.

faqs.question: What are the cut-off times at the Minang Geopark Run?
faqs.answer: In 2026 the limits were four hours for the half marathon, two and a half hours for the 10 km and an hour and a half for the 5 km. They are tighter than they look for this field: 13% of half-marathon finishers came in during the last 15 minutes before four hours, and 1.5% of 10 km finishers were outside the limit.

faqs.question: Is the Minang Geopark Run course hilly or off-road?
faqs.answer: Both, in part. The half marathon and 10 km run mostly on paved roads around Bukittinggi but include trail sections where the surface changes; the 5 km stays on roads. The city sits at about 930 m in the West Sumatra highlands, and the median half marathoner took 3:05 in 2026, a sign of a demanding course.

faqs.question: What is the weather like at the Minang Geopark Run?
faqs.answer: Cool and very humid. At the 6am start on 1 November 2026, Open-Meteo's historical model for Bukittinggi gives 19°C with 98% humidity and almost no wind, rising to 24°C by the 10am half-marathon cut-off, with light rain from about 7am. It is cooler than the coast, but sweat barely evaporates in air that wet.

faqs.question: How do you get to Bukittinggi for the Minang Geopark Run?
faqs.answer: In 2026 the organiser ran a DAMRI bus from Minangkabau International Airport and from the Masjid Raya Sumatera Barat in Padang to Pasa Ateh in Bukittinggi, at 11am and 4pm on the Friday and Saturday before the race, for Rp45,000 a person. Race packs had to be collected in person or by a friend before race day.

editorial_notes: Reinstated 2026-11-06: withdrawn 2026-09-28 because there was no earlier edition to review; official results for the 1 November 2026 race (NCI data dated 1 November 2026) now confirm it ran, and this review covers that edition. Field numbers are a Run SEA analysis of the NCI results (723 half-marathon and 916 10 km finishers; 5 km not included); start times are the gun times in those results. No earlier edition's results are held, so no year-on-year comparison. Weather is Open-Meteo historical model data for central Bukittinggi (grid elevation 935 m), used instead of airport METAR because Padang airport is at sea level. An Indonesia.travel listing gave 25 October 2026 as race day; the organiser's site and the results both say 1 November, which is used. The organiser's FAQ places the start at Jam Gadang and its race-day page on Jalan Perintis Kemerdekaan beside the race village; both are given. No route map or report of the 2026 race was found. Runners are not named. No rating.
